summary.headline: Schaeffler India says automotive demand is growing about 29-30% on GST 2.0 and localization is at 80%, with no explicit numbers on Q2 FY27 financials.
summary.overview: This was an investor group meeting (Sept 28, 2026), not a formal results call, so no quarterly financial figures were given. Management said automotive growth of roughly 29-30% was driven by GST 2.0 and BS-VI product transitions, while industrial growth was mixed, with infrastructure, steel, cement and railways strong and construction equipment and mining weak. Exports were framed as a by-product of localization, with management targeting 15-20% of revenue from exports. Management said the West Asia conflict raised input costs, with about 70% of cost increases typically recovered from customers, and that Vitesco's India integration has no timeline. E-mobility was described as loss-making and early-stage, with adoption under 5% today and about 15% expected by FY31.

financial_highlights.change: Stated as recent growth; period not specified
Expected to grow double digit for at least 6 months

financial_highlights.value: INR 350-400 crore by year end (questioner's figure)

financial_highlights.change: Up from 60-65% three to four years ago

segments.name: Automotive
segments.commentary: Growing about 29-30%, driven by GST 2.0 demand uplift and BS-VI new clutch and engine systems; management says the West Asia crisis affects automotive only through input costs, not demand.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Mixed: steel, cement and infrastructure strong, renewables (wind) growing, railways booming; construction equipment fell last year and mining has not recovered; industrial growth described as single digit.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: About 13-14% of revenue, expected to keep growing at double digits for at least six months; benefits from full electrification via insulation-coated traction motor bearings, which the company says it makes 100% locally.

segments.name: E-mobility
segments.commentary: Small base with strong growth on e-axle wins; currently loss-making, with e-axle content 100% imported and Phase 2 localization under way; industry EV adoption below 5% today.

segments.name: Wind
segments.commentary: Company says it holds about half the Indian wind bearings market; 1.6 m bearing produced last quarter for 6 MW turbines, and Savli Hall 3 under construction. No direct wind exports; about 85% of turbine output is exported by customers.

guidance_outlook: Exports expected to remain 15-20% of revenue as the domestic base grows 14-15%.
Localization will keep rising as an outcome of customer strategy; no fixed target set.
Shoolagiri greenfield spills into Phase 2, focused on passenger vehicle transmissions; no numbers given.
Two ICE engine and transmission production lines on their way to India.
Vitesco legal integration into the listed entity: no timeline as of now.
capex_capacity: Shoolagiri greenfield: first hall used as feeder line for existing plant; a production line from Europe is being moved in and a second hall is under construction.
E-axle localization at Phase 2 (sub-components assembled in India); end-of-line test line capacity 300,000 pieces vs demand of 85,000.
Wind: 1.6 m bearing produced for 6 MW turbines; Savli Hall 3 being built for wind-only expansion.
Railway production line capacity additions in progress.
Large-diameter wind bearings still imported because volumes of one or two pieces a month do not justify local production.
demand_pricing: Automotive demand supported by GST 2.0; management cites first-time car buyers overtaking repeat buyers as a sign the trend is intact.
Steel price increases passed through via contractual indexation; other inputs are negotiated and rupee depreciation makes recovery harder.
No price pressure seen so far in spherical and cylindrical bearings; more localization demand for large cylindricals.
Book-to-bill ratio is tracked and should stay above 1; project win probability tracked at 25/50/75% stages.
Competition in EV is intensifying (Bosch-Tata JV mentioned); the company says it is betting on ICE, hybrid and EV at once.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook given geopolitical tensions, and what is the geographic mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 50% Europe (intercompany), 25% Southeast Asia, with the rest China and the Americas; 13% of exports go to China. Exports are a by-product of localization, with the company expecting 15-20% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does the West Asia conflict affect costs and demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the crisis hits industrial exports and input costs (fuel, LPG), not automotive demand. About 70% of cost increases are typically recovered, with the remaining 30% absorbed by efficiencies.

qa_highlights.question: Where does Vitesco stand and is there an integration timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said there is no legal hurdle, but there is no timeline. Parent holds 74.13%, with 26% public; the group must integrate Vitesco entities worldwide first.

qa_highlights.question: How are EV economics and competition shaping up?
qa_highlights.answer: EV is loss-making at start; profitability depends on volume. EV adoption is below 5% today and about 15% by 2030-31 per internal research; hybrids are expected at about 15% by 2031.

qa_highlights.question: Is Vitesco's e-axle content imported, and what does Vitesco bring?
qa_highlights.answer: The e-axle is a Schaeffler portfolio product, with the CFO noting 100% import content at Phase 1. Vitesco adds BMS, sensors (NOx, knock) and power electronics; 800-volt capability is now under development.

qa_highlights.question: Is railway demand secular or lumpy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tendering-driven lumpiness will persist; electrification and the move to larger loads (Vande Bharat, freight Class K bearings) add structural demand.

risks_watch: Input cost pass-through: only about 70% recovery assumed, with rupee depreciation raising import costs for e-axle kits.
Industrial growth is single digit and construction equipment and mining remain weak.
E-mobility remains loss-making and import-dependent; competition is rising and adoption slow.
Vitesco legal integration has no timeline.
Geopolitical risk to export volumes, especially for bearings.
summary.management_tone: Confident on automotive and railways demand and on localization; cautious on e-mobility profitability and on the timing of the Vitesco integration. Management was evasive on numeric targets, repeatedly saying localization and export are outcomes rather than targets.
key_quotes: Hardevi Vazirani: Historically, usually 70% is recovered.
Harsha Kadam: Yes, there is no hurdle, as such.

Two ICE engine and transmission production lines coming to India

growth.why: No formal Q2 FY27 financials were given; the investor meeting cited ~29-30% automotive growth on GST 2.0 and a 14-15% domestic base growth outlook, with exports held at 15-20% of revenue, backed by partly specified capacity (Shoolagiri, Savli Hall 3, railway lines) but no quantified timelines or order-book figures.
